selector.champion: Primary invasive lobular breast carcinoma in heterotopic cutaneous breast tissue
selector.rationale: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, Indian file pattern, and positivity for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support this diagnosis. The association of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands with tumor cells further supports this choice.

registry.preferred_label: Primary invasive lobular breast carcinoma in heterotopic cutaneous breast tissue
registry.preferred_name: Primary invasive lobular breast carcinoma in heterotopic cutaneous breast tissue
support_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement. Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm.
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
